subject: Culture
title: Aid Politics
description: A micro-lesson that makes Aid Politics usable.

hook.text: US food aid once legally had to be grown in America and shipped on American vessels. Help came with strings.

buildup.text: Food aid can flood local markets, destroying the farmers it's supposed to help.

discovery.text: Economist Amartya Sen showed famines rarely come from food shortage—they come from power imbalances.

twist.text: Some countries refuse foreign food aid to protect national pride. North Korea has done this repeatedly.

climax.text: Giving food sounds simple and pure. In practice, it's tangled with politics, markets, and pride.

punchline.text: Even charity comes with a cost.

quiz.question: What did economist Amartya Sen argue about famines?
options: They result from power imbalances, not just food shortage
